URL: https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/andy-burnham-chagos-islands-deal-dead-7z708jxzq
The Times (Oliver Wright, Policy Editor) — published Thursday September 24 2026, 3.52pm BST

HEADLINE: Chagos deal is dead after Trump opposition, ministers believe
SUBHEAD: Whitehall source admitted that it would be hard for Andy Burnham to negotiate a new agreement that pleased both Mauritius and the US

FACTS:
- Plans to hand the Chagos Islands over to Mauritius are "dead" and will have to be renegotiated after President Trump reiterated his opposition, ministers believe.
- Senior government sources said ministers were under "no illusion" that the existing deal, signed by Sir Keir Starmer last year, could be resurrected. Officials are preparing to restart negotiations with Mauritius to try to reach a new deal acceptable to the White House.
- One source said it might be possible to make "cosmetic" changes to the agreement, under which Britain would hand the islands to Mauritius and lease back the joint US/UK base at Diego Garcia. They cited the deal Trump signed with Denmark reaffirming Copenhagen's sovereignty over Greenland.
- Terms of the original deal: Britain would pay £165 million a year for three years, then £120 million a year for 96 years, to lease back the joint US/UK airbase on Diego Garcia.
- The deal was announced by Starmer in October 2024 but delayed after Trump returned to the White House the following year. Trump was at first content with the plan; the US position changed after Starmer initially denied the US access to the base to attack Iranian positions over concerns the war was not legal.
- A UN vote in 2019, supported by Russia, China and Venezuela, awarded the islands to Mauritius, whose claim was then approved by a 13-1 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice.
- Trump made clear both in public and in private during his meeting with Burnham on Tuesday that his opposition stands.
- One Whitehall source said the agreement with Mauritius was made under a previous government and Burnham did not feel bound by it.

QUOTE (Whitehall/government source, per The Times): "We are going to have to go back to the drawing board. The challenge is keeping the Mauritians onboard."
QUOTE (Whitehall source, per The Times): "We will certainly try - but what we cannot do is keep the current deal on hold. That is not sustainable any longer."
QUOTE (Wes Streeting, Defence Secretary, speaking Wednesday to Times Radio): the deal "can't go ahead without American support".
QUOTE (Wes Streeting, Times Radio): while the International Court of Justice's ruling was "advisory now, there is a potential further course of legal action avenue open to the government of Mauritius".
QUOTE (Wes Streeting, Times Radio): Starmer's administration "got to a point where they clearly believed they did have the support of all parties involved" before concerns were raised in Washington.
QUOTE (Wes Streeting, Times Radio): "I'm not pretending that's an easy position and that resolving this is not going to be difficult. It is difficult and necessarily painstaking work, but it is necessary."
QUOTE (Wes Streeting, Times Radio): "The ostrich strategy of sticking our heads in the sand and hoping it [will] go away, I would caution, is not a wise strategy when it concerns one of the most sensitive national security assets we have anywhere in the world."

CORROBORATION: The Daily Telegraph, "Burnham's Chagos plan? Wait for Trump to leave office" (https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2026/09/24/burnhams-chagos-plan-wait-trump-leave-office/, 24 Sept 2026) reports Whitehall hopes to ride out the US president's term before handing £35bn to Mauritius for a 99-year lease of the Diego Garcia base. BBC: "UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC" (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck3wjy3pdwdno).
